hook.line: News is coming at Tomás from every side this week, and silence reads as not caring. A Colombian reacts out loud, fast, in two or three words.
hook.en: Long time no see! (to a friend)

examples.en: How good to see you, don Hernando!
You look lovely! (to a woman, a friend)

rule:
You already react with *¡Qué bonito!* and *¡Qué pena!* Now stretch it.

*¡Qué* + describing word + thing: *¡Qué bonita sorpresa!* English says what a lovely surprise; Spanish has no a.
*¡Qué bien*, *¡Qué rápido* + verb: *¡Qué bien cocina Vale!* The verb comes straight after, and the person goes to the end.
*¡Qué bueno* + verb: *¡Qué bueno verte!*
*¡Cuánto!* for so much, so many. It matches the thing: *cuánto tiempo*, *cuánta gente*, *cuántos regalos*, *cuántas flores*.

The accent on *qué* and *cuánto* is what makes it a reaction. Without it, *que* is just that, the word in *Que te vaya bien*. And the marks at both ends tell you it's a reaction, not a question: *¡Cuánta gente!* (so many people) against *¿Cuánta gente viene?* (how many people are coming?).

Colombians love a short *¡Tan lindo!* for anything sweet.
smallPrint: Teachers call these exclamatives (*oraciones exclamativas*). In a longer pattern, *¡Qué día tan largo!*, *tan* goes before the describing word.

options: How well it's going for you!
You look lovely! (to a woman, a friend)
You look lovely! (to a man, a friend)
Are you well? (to a woman, a friend)

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *cuánto* or *cuánta* and type the whole reaction: *¡___ gente!* (So many people!)
Pick *que* or *qué* and type the whole reaction: *¡___ bueno verte!* (How good to see you!)
React in Spanish: So many presents!
React in Spanish: What a lovely surprise! (use *bonita*)
yourTurn.why: No word for a: just *qué*, then the describing word, then the thing.

yourTurn.prompt: React in Spanish: Long time no see! (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: Literally so much time without seeing you; *tiempo* is an *el* word, so *cuánto*.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn the plain statement into a reaction: *Vale cocina muy bien.*
yourTurn.why: *Qué bien* goes first, the verb right after, and Vale moves to the end.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn the question into a reaction: *¿Cuánta comida hay?* (So much food!)
yourTurn.why: Same words, new marks: *¡ !* makes it a reaction.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Without the accent, *que* is just that; a reaction needs *qué*.
English says what a surprise, but Spanish drops the a.
*Cuánto* matches the thing, and *gente* is a *la* word.
The verb comes right after *qué bien*; the person goes to the end.

personal: Think of the last good news you heard and react to it in Spanish with *¡Qué...!* or *¡Cuánto...!*
